sections.synopsis: An upper level low will continue to weaken into Saturday, with drying and cooling conditions through the weekend. Upper level ridging will build through the first half of next week for continued dry conditions, before additional systems look to arrive by midweek.
sections.short_term:
Showers continue to taper off this evening, with a few lingering showers over western Washington. An upper level low will start to move southwards and weaken, taking away the showery influence over western Washington. We'll start a dry and cool trend heading into the weekend, with afternoon temps staying in the low 50s. Overnight lows, especially tonight into Saturday morning, will cool, with areas in the Southwest Interior seeing below freezing temperatures in the upper 20s and low 30s. Therefore, a Freeze Warning is in effect for those locations. A Frost Advisory has also been issued for the northern Olympic Peninsula and north of Seattle as temperatures are expected to range between 32 to 36 early Saturday. Take the proper precautions to protect vegetation if needed. Besides the cold temperatures, should be dry for any trick or treaters.

Dry and cool conditions through Sunday over the region. Overnight low temperatures will be flirting with freezing temperatures as well, in the low 30s.

Mazurkiewicz
sections.long_term: Ensemble guidance remains in reasonably good agreement for the first half of next week with an upper ridge remaining generally over the region for the start of next week. This will maintain mostly dry conditions, though a portion of ensemble members bring a weak disturbance into the ridge enough to bring some light precipitation chances (20-30%) west of Puget Sound. Another weak disturbance brings similar chances toward midweek. A more notable shift in the pattern becomes more likely late in the week with a stronger front approaching Western Washington, but it's worth noting that there's significantly increasing spread in the potential evolution of the pattern by that time. Cullen
sections.marine:
Weak surface low pressure over the coastal waters will remain in place into Saturday before dissipating as high pressure builds across the interior of Western Washington early in the coming week. Southeasterly winds over the coastal waters this afternoon will reach 15 to 20 kts at times, but should remain under small craft advisory criteria. Winds look to remain generally benign and light across the area waters through the first half of next week.

Coastal seas 4 to 6 feet through the weekend. Seas will build to slowly build late Sunday into Monday, back around 10 to 11 feet as a larger swell train approaches.

Mazurkiewicz

sections.synopsis: Light to moderate trade winds will produce modest showers over most windward areas into early Saturday, while lingering moisture produces wetter conditions on windward Big Island. A disturbance aloft may trigger isolated heavy showers over the state late Saturday. The tail end of a front will move down the island chain late Sunday through Monday, bringing breezy northeasterly trades and drier air in its wake. Then breezy easterly trades will bring periods of windward and mauka showers through the rest of the week.
sections.short_term:
Stubborn shallow moisture continues to produce enhanced cloud cover over the island chain with somewhat wet conditions lingering on windward Big Island. The surface trough that affected the state during the past few days is now just southeast of Big Island and drifting away, but deeper moisture pooled around this feature remains hung up on windward Big Island, where showers will gradually diminish in intensity and coverage overnight. Across the remainder of the island chain, light to moderate trades will produce mainly scattered showers along windward slopes. Lingering moisture from the above mentioned trough is manifested as increased cloud cover, with deeper moisture lingering to the southwest and west of Kauai waters.

There is an unusually high degree of disagreement between the latest runs of the GFS and ECMWF for Saturday. The GFS is maintaining a drier, light to moderate trade wind flow, even as an upper level trough approaches from the northwest. Meanwhile, the ECMWF has the upper level trough tapping the lingering moisture just southwest and west of Kauai and producing higher chances of afternoon and evening showers on Kauai and Oahu. We will be taking a closer look at the guidance overnight to determine if adjustments need to be made in the forecast.
sections.prev_discussion:
Issued at 351 PM HST Fri Oct 30 2026 Radar and satellite imagery show moderate trade winds focusing low clouds and showers over windward and mauka areas across the state this afternoon as trades finally fill in across the Big Island. With abundant tropical moisture lingering over the region, isolated heavy downpours will remain possible over the Big Island through this evening, where the greatest moisture and instability persist. Heading into Saturday, model soundings show more stable conditions developing, leading to a more typical trade wind pattern through the weekend with shallow passing windward and mauka showers.

The next pattern change arrives late Sunday into Monday as an upper-level trough sweeps across the north-central Pacific and the tail end of a frontal boundary attempts to push down the island chain. An increase in windward and mauka showers can be expected ahead of and along this boundary, with breezy northeast winds and drier air filtering in its wake as high pressure builds to the north. This will bring welcome relief from this week's muggy conditions, with dew points projected to drop into the lower 60s on Monday and Tuesday.

The surface high north of the state will become elongated as a broad low pressure system tracks across the North Pacific, maintaining breezy easterly trades across the islands through the workweek. As batches of moisture filter through on the trades, periods of enhanced windward and mauka showers can be expected. One of these upticks in shower activity looks to occur midweek as increased moisture moves in on the trade wind flow and a weak mid-level shortwave trough adds some instability as it sweeps across from the east.

By next weekend, noticeable model spread emerges between the GFS and ECMWF. While trade winds look to persist, questions remain regarding their strength and how much moisture theyll bring to the area. The GFS continues to hint at a tropical cyclone developing far southeast of the state, whereas the ECMWF does not. The National Hurricane Center continues to monitor this area, maintaining a medium (40 percent) chance of development over the next 7 days.
sections.marine:
High pressure to the north will bring moderate to fresh trades to the region into the weekend. As the trades build, a Small Craft Advisory will likely be needed for the typical windier waters, and an incoming north-northwest swell will bring seas in excess of 10 feet to exposed waters.

The current small, short period north-northeast swell will maintain small surf along north-facing shores into Saturday. A larger, long-period northwest swell is expected to arrive late Saturday and will bring advisory level surf to north and west facing shores exposed to the swell Sunday into Monday. The swell is expected to shift slightly more northerly and may briefly build further on Monday before dropping Tuesday. Depending on the exact direction, a Marine Weather Statement may eventually need to be issued due to the potential for harbor surges at Kahului and Hilo during that time.

The current small, medium period south swell will gradually decline through the weekend. During the first half of next week, south shore surf will return to below seasonal averages. East- facing shores will continue to be boosted due to the wrap from the north and southerly swells. As the larger north swell builds in Sunday night and Monday, the wrap from that will have the potential for advisory level surf during that time.
